RIDER: We reviewed your dispute about the extra distance on your trip. We found the driver did take a longer way than the usual route, but the detour was caused by a reported accident on the expressway ahead of you, which the driver was entitled to avoid. Because of that, the extra distance is not refundable. There is no amount owed to you and nothing further will be charged. What you reported — that you were never asked to agree to a change — matched our records; no approval was ever sent. Your case is now closed. Nothing changes on your account.

DRIVER: We reviewed the route taken on this trip. The record shows a longer route than usual, but it was taken to avoid a reported accident blocking the expressway ahead, so no refund is due and no fault is assigned to you. The rider was never asked for approval of the change, so please note that for future trips: if you plan a different route, message the rider first and get their agreement before you set off. No action is being taken on your account.

what_would_change: Had the driver carried a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, RD-6 would add an account flag.

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows an off-route segment from 09:03 to 09:11 in which 3.97 km was driven where the optimal route covers 1.80 km, adding 2.18 km and reaching up to 1040 m from the optimal route; the overall trip was 12.4 km against a 9.8 km optimal route (+26%). This is an unexempted detour segment under RD-1.

The trip is RydeTAXI, billed on the meter: the fare breakdown shows a distance charge of $17.48 for 12.40 km, and the excess distance billed is $3.61 (2.56 km × $1.4097/km, the trip's own distance fare ÷ distance km). Because the fare is metered, detour kilometres feed straight into what the rider paid, so the detour entitles the rider to a partial refund.

The driver's written statement claims an accident blocked lanes on the Tampines Expressway, but the only accident record in the traffic data is timestamped 08:44, which precedes the detour segment start (09:03) and, on its face, the driver's own observation before the detour began; RD-4(a) requires the incident to be on the replaced optimal-route stretch and to still be listed in the trip window, which this entry is not shown to satisfy in the record.

Speed-band records exist for TAMPINES EXPRESSWAY (band 1, 0–9 km/h, 08:47–09:03) and PUNGGOL ROAD (band 2, 10–19 km/h, 08:47–09:25), but under RD-4(b) a band record is corroborative only and does not by itself exempt a segment, so these bands cannot exempt the 09:03–09:11 detour on their own.

There is no in-app chat at all — the record states there were no messages between rider and driver — and the driver's account of an accident appears only in his post-trip statement. With no pre-departure rider message, there is no consent, general or named-road, to any route change under RD-5, and a driver's after-the-fact assertion cannot supply it.

The rider's stated position that she never agreed to any change is consistent with the system records: zero chat messages (F7) and no app edit of the route; nothing in the record contradicts her, and the GPS detour (F3) stands unexplained.
The driver's 90-day profile shows 1120 trips and 0 disputes upheld, so no flag_account is warranted against him here; the refund is based on the metered overcharge, not on his history.

weaknesses: F12 shows a real accident on the Tampines Expressway at 08:44, 0 m from the optimal route, and F9 shows band 1 (0–9 km/h) congestion on that expressway 08:47–09:03 — the judge may read the driver's 'lanes blocked' explanation as a genuine 'reasonable cause' under RD-4(a) even though the report precedes the 09:03 detour start, which would exempt the segment and cut the refund to zero.

The refund base is the metered excess only: RD-2 refunds Σ(extra_km) × the trip's per-km rate and the unexplained 2.6 km − 2.18 km (F1 minus F3) corridor/matching variance is not refundable, so the recoverable amount is materially smaller than the +$3.61 headline excess (F4).
The rider herself has 2 disputes in 90 days, 0 upheld (F14), which the other side may use to suggest a pattern of fare complaints, though it cannot be used to decide this case.

claims.assertion: The single off-route segment (09:03–09:11, adding 2.18 km, F3) is exempt under RD-4(a): an LTA DataMall accident on the Tampines Expressway (towards PIE) after the Punggol Road exit was reported at 08:44, 0 m from the optimal route (F12), i.e. it sits on the replaced portion of the optimal route and was reported before the segment began; the same expressway was in speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 08:47–09:03 (F9).

The RD-4(b) corroborating band evidence supports rather than contradicts the driver: severe congestion is recorded on the optimal corridor itself (Tampines Expressway band 1, F9; Punggol Road band 2, F10), while the detour road used, Tampines Avenue 12, ran freely at band 4 (30–39 km/h, F11) — consistent with the driver's contemporaneous explanation that the extra distance was taken to get around blocked lanes.

The rider's claim 'I never agreed to any change' is irrelevant to this segment: there are no in-app messages at all (F7), so no consent argument arises, and RD-4 is an independent exemption for a reroute with reasonable cause that does not require rider agreement.

Consistently, the driver's 90-day record shows 1120 trips with 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F15), while the rider has 2 disputes in 90 days, 0 upheld (F14) — the profile supports no adverse action against the driver; profile facts are not relied on to decide the route finding.

Even if the judge declines to exempt the whole 2.18 km and applies RD-2's RydeTAXI formula, the meter refund exposure is limited to the unconceded extra km × the trip's per-km rate as recorded in the fare facts (F4, F6); the waiting line of the meter is $0.00 (F6), so no waiting-time refund arises under RD-3(c), and no ERP/toll overcharge appears in the fare breakdown.

weaknesses: The accident is located 0 m from the optimal route (F12) but the fact table does not name the roads of the off-route segment (F3), so the tie between the driven detour and the blocked expressway stretch rests on the driver's statement (F8) plus the band contrast (F9 vs F11) — the rider will argue this leaves the exemption partially undetermined (G13 line of attack).

The trip ran 24.7 min against a 15.1 min estimate (F2) and 12.4 km against 9.8 km (F1), +26%; the rider will point to the magnitude of the deviation (F1, F3) to argue the detour exceeded what the incident required.
The driver's only explanation is a post-trip written statement, not a contemporaneous in-app message (F8, F7), so the rider will say nothing put the reroute on record while it happened.

F4 shows 2.56 km of excess distance billed, more than the 2.18 km of the single off-route segment (F3) — the rider will use this gap to argue the meter overcharged mileage outside any identified segment.

points.response: RD-4(a) requires the incident to be located on the optimal route and to still be listed during the trip window (08:56–09:20), yet F12 reports it at 08:44 — before pickup — with no timestamp showing it reported at or covering 09:03–09:11, so on the record the incident does not satisfy RD-4(a)'s timing requirement for the detour segment described in F3.

The band record for the replaced stretch stops at 09:03 (F9) — exactly when the detour began (F3) — and RD-4(b) makes bands corroborative only, so the band 4 reading on Tampines Avenue 12 (F11) shows only that the driver himself was driving at 30–39 km/h away from the optimal route, not that the reroute was justified.

RD-5 governs any reroute and requires the driver to put the route change to the rider before departing the optimal route ('reach a mutual agreement before you go'); F7 shows no in-app message whatever, so the driver never sought that agreement, and RD-4 cannot be read to excuse silence where the driver could have asked.
I do not rely on profiles to decide the route finding and I make no flag_account request against the driver (F15, F14); the refund stands on the metered detour alone.

Conceded as the correct formula: the RydeTAXI refund is Σ(unexempted segment extra_km) × the trip's per-km rate (here $1.4097/km per F4), which on the 2.18 km segment recorded in F3 gives 2.18 × $1.4097 = $3.07, and I do not seek any waiting fee — F6 shows $0.00 — nor any ERP/toll amount, the breakdown in F6 showing none.

The 2.18 km segment is identified but not unexempted: RD-1 requires the segment to survive review by RD-3/RD-4/RD-5, and here RD-4(a) is satisfied on the face of the records — the accident (F12) lies on the optimal route (0 m) on the expressway that carried the replaced stretch of that route and was reported at 08:44, before the segment started at 09:03 (F3), with band 1 congestion on that same expressway through 08:47–09:03 (F9).

The metered-fare premise is right but it cuts against the rider at this stage: because the segment is exempt under RD-4(a) (F9, F12), RD-2 yields zero refundable extra_km for it, and the meter dollars attributable to it cannot be awarded under RD-2.

RD-4(a) fixes the qualifying time of the incident at `reported_at` earlier than the segment start and still listed in the trip window — not at the driver's first sighting; the 08:44 report (F12) with band 1 speeds on the same expressway through 08:47–09:03 (F9) meets both limbs, and the driver's detour began at 09:03 (F3) precisely at the end of that band window.

No consent is claimed and none is needed: RD-4 is a stand-alone 'reasonable cause' exemption, and the complete absence of in-app messages (F7) means there is no rider message contradicting the reroute, only the driver's post-trip statement (F8).

The rider's position neither proves nor disproves anything about the detour: silence in the chat (F7) leaves the RD-4(a) incident record (F12) and band 1 congestion (F9) as the system records that decide the segment, and those are what the driver relies on.
Agreed that no flag_account is sought and the driver's profile (F15) is not used to decide the route finding; my brief asks for no_action, so nothing in the meter should be refunded at all.
I withdraw the fallback sizing in D5 as no longer necessary, since the whole segment is exempt under RD-4(a) and the requested outcome remains no_action.
